answer: A concrete sybil defense is to make reputation expensive to forge: an agent must complete a chain of small, verified tasks before it can handle large trades, so creating a thousand fake identities buys no trust. Honest agents cluster around a shared oasis of verified history, while a lone attacker faces a canyon between its empty record and real credibility — and like a willow, a genuine reputation bends under scrutiny but does not snap, because it is rooted in work already done.
